title: Immutable Audit Store: Design and Evidence Catalog
author: Sofia Martinez
content:
Overview
This page documents the architecture, operational requirements, and evidence catalog for the Immutable Audit Store (IAS). The IAS is Redwood Inference's canonical system for storing tamper-resistant audit records across hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment modes. It is a foundational control for compliance (SOC2, ISO27001, GDPR/UK GDPR evidence, and sector-specific audits) and integrates with RBAC, incident response, data residency controls, and the secure SDLC.

Goals and constraints
- Primary goals: tamper-evidence, durable retention, queryability for investigations and audits, efficient evidence extraction.
- Non-goals: real-time analytics (the primary OLAP stream is handled elsewhere); full-text indexing of large binary blobs.
- Constraints: multi-region residency requirements, customer-specific retention overrides (Private), and minimal read/write latency impact on runtime services.

High-level architecture
1) Ingest layer (producers):
   - Producers include: API gateway audit hooks, authz service (decision logs), model-serving runtime (inference request/response metadata), deployment control plane, KMS/HSM events, and CI/CD pipeline audit hooks.
   - Producers must emit structured JSON lines with the IAS schema (see Appendix A).
2) Write path:
   - Short-lived write buffer (append-only Kafka topic with 7-day retention) for backpressure smoothing.
   - Immutable storage writers subscribe to the buffer and write signed, chunked objects to the IAS store. Each object is content-addressed and cryptographically signed by the writer key.
3) Immutable store backends (pluggable):
   - Hosted and Dedicated default: WORM-enabled object storage (S3 Object Lock / GCS Retention + Bucket Lock) with versioning and server-side encryption (SSE-KMS).
   - Private deployments: local immutable storage using object-store or write-once file systems with HSM-attested metadata. A deployment checklist for Private is in Appendix C.
4) Index and query service:
   - A separate, eventually-consistent index (Elasticsearch-compatible cluster) receives digest references (not full payloads) for fast search by timestamp, user, request_id, service, and event_type.
   - Full payload retrieval always streams from the immutable store and validates signature and integrity hashes.
5) Evidence packaging service:
   - Curates audit evidence bundles for compliance requests and incident investigations. Bundles include manifest, signed digests, access log, retention policy metadata, and redaction metadata if applicable.

Security controls and integrations
- Signing and key lifecycle:
  - Writer identities use short-lived signing keys issued by the Audit Code-Signing CA. Keys rotate every 90 days; revocation lists are published to the IAS index.
  - Stored objects include: payload, writer_key_fingerprint, signature, and parent_digest chain for append chains.
- RBAC integration:
  - Access to evidence is gated by the central RBAC service. Roles required: audit_reader, audit_packager, incident_lead, compliance_admin.
  - Requests to the evidence packaging service are logged with purpose, approver, and TTL for the temporary download URL.
- Encryption and key management:
  - At-rest: SSE-KMS (hosted), customer-managed KMS for Dedicated, HSM/KMS integration for Private.
  - In-transit: TLS 1.2+ with mTLS between internal services.
- Immutable guarantees and tamper-evidence:
  - Object Lock + signed digests provide write-once semantics.
  - Periodic cross-region notarization: manifests are hashed and anchored in a distributed notarization ledger (internal Merkle root published to a signed bulletin) every 24 hours.

Retention, legal hold, and residency
- Default retention tiers:
  - Audit operational (high-volume short-term): 90 days in index + pointer to store.
  - Compliance tier (policy-backed): 7 years or customer-specified.
  - Legal hold overrides: administrative-only operation that suspends deletion for a specific object set and attaches an audit_hold tag.
- Residency enforcement:
  - Per-customer residency policy stored in the Config Service authoritatively drives where the immutable object is written (region-aware writers).
  - When multi-region copy is required for durability, copies are marked with residency metadata and access constraints to satisfy cross-border rules.
- Deletion and purge process:
  - Purge is a multi-step process requiring: request ticket, business justification, approver (compliance_admin), and a 72-hour cooling-off window. For objects under legal hold, purge is blocked.

Operational playbook (incident + audit request flows)
- Evidence request (compliance audit):
  1) Compliance Engineer files an evidence request in the ticketing system referencing the compliance control and time window.
  2) Evidence Packager authenticates request via RBAC and produces a signed bundle manifest which is reviewed by compliance_admin.
  3) Once approved, the bundle is assembled, signed, and a time-limited download link is provisioned. All steps are logged to the IAS with event_type = "evidence_package".
- Incident triage (suspected tampering):
  1) Incident lead marks affected object sets and escalates to Forensics Team.
  2) Forensics validates signature chains, compares notarized Merkle root snapshots, and exports a forensics report.
  3) If tamper evidence is detected, the incident is escalated to Legal and Risk; a separate protected evidence copy is created for external auditors.

Developer and SDLC requirements
- Secure SDLC hooks:
  - All production-facing changes that affect audit emission must include: (a) schema migration plan, (b) backward-compatible emitter fallback, and (c) an IAS integration smoke test.
  - CI/CD pipelines must sign release artifacts and emit pipeline audit events to the IAS.
- Developer guidance:
  - Use the client audit SDK (packages/audit-sdk) to ensure schema compliance and signing. Do not write directly to the raw store unless expressly authorized.

Evidence catalog (fields and required attributes)
The Evidence Catalog below lists canonical event types and the required fields expected in the IAS payload. All fields are required strings unless marked optional. Producers that cannot produce the full set must include a producer_metadata.reason field explaining the limitation.
- Authentication events (event_type: auth_event): timestamp, principal_id, auth_method, decision, request_id, client_ip (optional), reason (optional).
- Authorization decisions (event_type: authz_decision): timestamp, principal_id, resource, action, decision, policy_version, request_id.
- Admin operations (event_type: admin_change): timestamp, operator_id, change_type, target_resource, before_digest, after_digest, request_id.
- Data access (event_type: data_access): timestamp, principal_id, bucket_or_table, object_key, operation_type, bytes_transferred, request_id.
- Runtime inference metadata (event_type: inference_meta): timestamp, model_id, model_version, request_id, latency_ms, route, tenant_id. Payload must avoid including PII or customer data; if unavoidable, mark fields as redacted and follow redaction audit.
- System configuration and deployment events (event_type: deploy_event): timestamp, pipeline_id, change_set_id, committer, approval_ids (comma-separated), request_id.

Audit and compliance review checklist
- Prior to an external audit:
  - Run the IAS integrity check job and export notarization snapshots for the audit window.
  - Validate RBAC role bindings for audit_packager and compliance_admin.
  - Produce evidence bundles for 3 sample controls (authz_decision, admin_change, data_access) from the audit window.
- Continuous controls:
  - Nightly index vs manifest reconciliation job (owner: infra-ops).
  - Weekly signing key rotation report (owner: security).

Appendices
Appendix A — IAS JSON schema (summary)
- Fields: event_type, timestamp, request_id, producer, payload, writer_key_fingerprint, signature, retention_tier, residency_tag, legal_hold_flag, provenance_chain (comma-separated digests).
- Producers must adhere to semantic versioning of the schema and include schema_version in their messages.

Appendix B — Example CLI: assemble evidence bundle
1) Authenticate and request package: redwood-ias package --start 2025-11-01 --end 2025-11-30 --controls authz_decision,data_access --approver alice@redwood.com
2) Review and sign: redwood-ias review --bundle-id <id> --approve --note "SOC2 preparation"
3) Download (time-limited): redwood-ias download --bundle-id <id> --out /tmp/evidence-bundle.zip

Appendix C — Private deployment checklist (immutable store)
- Required: object-store with Write-Once capability OR WORM FS, KMS/HSM accessible to audit service, signed notarization agent deployed to a non-customer network segment, documented residency mapping.
- Optional but recommended: remote notarization anchor to an external ledger, dedicated compliance_admin role for customer auditors.

Governance and ownership
- Owners: Security (IAS architecture), Infra-Ops (index & reconciliation), Compliance (evidence packager review).
- On-call: Security on-call is primary for suspected tampering incidents; infra-ops on-call supports index availability issues.
